cards.text: Jesus has been staying across the Jordan, after the Jews in Jerusalem tried to seize Him (John 10:22-40). Meanwhile, a man named Lazarus is sick, back home in the village of his sisters, Mary and Martha. This is the same Mary who will one day anoint the Lord with perfume and wipe His feet with her hair.

cards.question: Lazarus, the brother of Mary and Martha, is sick. Which village does he live in?

cards.text: So the sisters send word to Jesus: "Lord, the one You love is sick." Short and clear, friend, which is more than I can say for MY texts, which run three paragraphs and STILL forget the point.

cards.question: When Jesus hears that Lazarus is sick, He says this sickness will end in death.
Jesus says Lazarus's sickness won't end in death. What does He say the sickness is for?

answers.text: A test of the sisters' faith

cards.text: Then the story stops to make one thing clear: Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.

cards.question: When Jesus hears Lazarus is sick, He sets out for Bethany right away.
Instead of leaving for Bethany, Jesus stays where He is for ___ days.

cards.text: Then He tells the disciples, "Let us go back to Judea." That's the region around Jerusalem, where the Jews just tried to seize Him (John 10:22-39).

cards.question: The disciples call Jesus Rabbi and push back on going to Judea. What do they remind Him?

answers.text: The Jews just tried to stone Him
The sisters told Him to stay away

cards.text: The disciples are wary of Judea, and honestly, same: my oven singed my mustache ONE time and I STILL open it from across the room. Jesus answers with a question: "Are there not twelve hours of daylight?"

cards.question: Jesus goes on: whoever walks in the daytime won't ___, because he sees by the light of this world.

cards.text: But whoever walks at night will stumble, because he has no light. After He says this, Jesus tells them their friend Lazarus has fallen asleep.

cards.question: Jesus says their friend Lazarus has fallen asleep. What does He say He's going to do?

answers.text: Go there and wake him up
Let him rest a while longer
Pray for him from right here

cards.question: The disciples reply that if Lazarus is sleeping, he will get better.
The disciples thought Jesus meant actual sleep. What was He really talking about?

cards.text: So Jesus tells them plainly: Lazarus is dead.

cards.question: Jesus says He's glad He wasn't there when Lazarus died. Whose sake does He say that's for?
Jesus says He's glad He wasn't there, so that the disciples may believe.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "But let us go to him." And Thomas, one of the disciples, also called Didymus, turns to the others.

cards.question: Judea is where they just tried to stone Jesus. What does Thomas tell his fellow disciples?

answers.text: Let us also go so that we may die with Him
Let us stay here until it is safe to travel
Let us send word to the sisters before we go

cards.text: And that's where we'll pause. Hold onto your apron, friend, because this story is far from over.

findings.problem: The setup gives away the answer to card 10. Card 9 (and card 1) say the Jews in Jerusalem just tried to seize Jesus. Card 10 then asks what the disciples remind Him of, and the right answer is 'The Jews just tried to stone Him.' The setup almost states the answer, and it rules out both wrong answers (guards on the roads, the sisters telling Him to stay away). The two cards also cite different ranges for the same event: John 10:22-40 on card 1 and John 10:22-39 on card 9.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card opens by retelling John 11:8 ('The disciples are wary of Judea'). Stop 1 card 10 already covered that verse. Because of this recap, the card cites John 11:8-9, which reaches outside Stop 2's own range of John 11:9-16.

rule.text:
Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
- No recap cards.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin is only mildly funny. Across 22 cards there are just two jokes (Stop 1 card 3 and Stop 2 card 1). Most story cards read as plain narration with no reaction, comparison or disbelief, including Stop 1 card 6 and Stop 2 cards 3, 7 and 10. Two moments that could easily carry a real laugh without muddying a fact get no reaction at all: the disciples taking 'asleep' literally (John 11:12-13) and Thomas's 'so that we may die with Him' (John 11:16).

rule.text: **But he is FUNNY.** Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The joke has Papa Dorin sending his own texts ('MY texts, which run three paragraphs'). The docs let him use phones and texts for comparisons, and they let his jokes make up small moments and habits around his bakery. They also say he never adds anything new to his world, and that he lives alone on the cookie planet. It's unclear whether Papa Dorin texting someone adds something new to his world.
findings.question: Can Papa Dorin's self-deprecating jokes show him doing everyday adult things himself, like sending texts? Or should those everyday comparisons stay about other people, keeping his own habits to the bakery?
